newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IBM to invest more than $350 mln in Ireland.
newsitem.headline: IBM to invest more than $350 mln in Ireland.

text.p: Information technology company IBM will invest more than $350 million in creating a campus-type strategic operating site in Dublin, the Irish government said on Thursday.
The IBM investment, which is backed by Irish industrial development agency IDA Ireland, should directly generate 2,850 new jobs over the next five years, a government statement said.
The first phase of the project will involve the manufacture of memory storage disks while later phases of the project will include a customer support telecentre and software manufacturing.
Ireland has announced 46 major new investments in electronics in 1996, involving investment in excess of 800 million punts and creating more than 12,000 new jobs.
